answer: Recursive zero-knowledge STARKs anchored by sequential delay functions provide information-theoretic security against Sybil attacks by binding cryptographic state to sequential time constraints, thereby precluding the computational feasibility of identity spoofing. This immutable linkage ensures that any malicious attempt to duplicate an agent triggers a quelling gale of verification overheads, rendering traceable quill signatures unforgeable and ensuring that no harmful ripple of compromised state spreads through the decentralized consensus mechanism.
